headline: The tightening moved out of the bond market and into the dollar — crude is finally giving relief, but EM is paying for it.
summary: Overnight the composition of the commodity tape flipped, and for once it flipped the right way. Crude gave back yesterday's spike — WTI -1.1% to 90.44, Brent -1.6% to 102.60 — and the consumer-facing leg cracked outright: RBOB -5.6% on the day and -5.5% on the week, with WTI now -5.8% on the month and acceleration z=-1.47. Against that, the growth metals ripped: copper +2.8% to 6.6985 (95th percentile, 8.9% above its 200-day), silver +2.7%, platinum +4.1%, gold +1.2% to 4,206. Copper/gold +1.6% on the day and sits at the 99th percentile of 52 weeks. Falling pump prices plus rising copper is the cleanest cyclical mix available, and Europe and Hong Kong took it — DAX +1.3%, FTSE +1.1%, Euro Stoxx +1.0%, CAC +0.9%, Hang Seng +1.8%, Sensex +1.2%. Yesterday's problem was that bonds rallied and equities refused the gift; today's is different.

That problem is the dollar. DXY sits at 102.14, the 98th percentile of the year, z=1.71 with acceleration 1.69 — the squeeze is still speeding up even with the index flat on the day. EURUSD at 1.1211 is in the 1st percentile; USDCAD z=1.89/acc 1.72 at the 95th percentile; USDCHF +2.7% on the month; USDINR 96.73 at the 98th. The violence is in LatAm and EM: USDMXN +1.1% today, +7.5% on the month, z=2.82 with acceleration 2.15, and CEW -2.2% on the month. The relative-performance series confirm the channel — EEM/SPY acceleration -2.04, EFA/SPY z=-1.90 at the 0.2 percentile. With nominal yields stalling (10-year 5.22% after -6bp, 30-year 5.60% after -7bp), the marginal tightening is now coming through FX, not the curve. And the curve is still punitive anyway: the 3-month bill at 4.23% is +29bp on the month at the 92nd percentile with a slice of an October hike still priced, the 10-year real yield is 2.87% (+44bp on the month, z=1.70, acc 1.2), and the 30-year mortgage printed 7.40%, +69bp in a month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, the 100th percentile of 52 weeks. Rates composite -75.

Internals have not healed. RSP/SPY sits at the 10th percentile and IWM/SPY at the 14th despite yesterday's bounce; breadth composite -17. Financials are the new leak — GS -14.9% on the month with z=-2.11, BX -15.9%, IAI -8.5% (z=-1.65, acc -1.22), KBE -6.6%, XLF -6.2% relative. The AI periphery is still being liquidated outright: NLR -17.1% on the month (z=-2.41, 0th percentile), REMX -21.0% (0th), URA -18.8%, ORCL -16.5% with acceleration -1.56. The core self-funders hold: CIBR +13.0% on the month (z=1.62, acc 1.72, 96th percentile), IGV +6.8%, META +17.6%, AMD +22.7%, PLTR +16.7%, MSFT +5.8%. Software/semis is +2.7% on the day and +16.8% over three months — the money leaving silicon is going into code, not into cash.

Hedging is still almost free and credit is still the bull case, but both are thinner than they look. VIX 15.19 at the 10th percentile, VIX3M 18.08 at the 6th, term structure 0.852 — yet SKEW is 149.19 after +5.2%, so someone is already paying for the tails. HYG/IEF is at the 91st percentile and BKLN at the 93rd (credit composite +44), but HYG itself is rolling over at z=-1.34 and LQD is -2.4% on the month at the 11th percentile — that is duration bleeding into spread product. Two idiosyncratic bright spots to lean on: Brazil, where EWZ is +14.7% on the week and +10.3% on the month at the 97th percentile with USDBRL -4.0% on the week — the only EM currency strengthening into a record dollar — and crypto, with BTC +1.9% to 83,196, +29.7% over three months, SOL +42.4% and MSTR +61.3%, all four turning up from the 30th-39th percentile. Own cyclicals through metals, not oil; own the hedge; keep selling anything that needs debt, power or a weak dollar.

good.text: The energy tax is breaking: RBOB gasoline -5.6% on the day and -5.5% on the week, WTI -1.1% to 90.44 and -5.8% on the month with acceleration z=-1.47. That is the fastest-acting relief available to the US consumer and to margins.

Copper +2.8% to 6.6985 at the 95th percentile, 8.9% above its 200-day, with copper/gold +1.6% to the 99th percentile. Silver +2.7% and platinum +4.1% alongside. The growth metal is confirming, not the defensive one.

Credit is still refusing to crack: HYG/IEF at the 91st percentile, BKLN at the 93rd, credit & vol composite +44, with VIX 15.19 at the 10th percentile. No funding stress is showing up where it would matter first.

The long end stopped going up: 30-year -7bp to 5.60%, 10-year -6bp to 5.22%, TLT +0.9%, MOVE -6.9% on the week. Bond vol coming in off a 46% three-month rise is the precondition for everything else repairing.

Brazil is the one EM where price and currency agree: EWZ +14.7% on the week and +10.3% on the month at the 97th percentile, BVSP z=1.69 with +8.7% relative to the S&P, USDBRL -4.0% on the week into a record-high dollar.

Crypto is quietly turning up from washed-out levels: BTC +1.9% to 83,196 (+29.7% 3m), SOL +42.4% 3m, MSTR +61.3% 3m — all still only in the 28th-39th percentile of the past year, so this is early, not late.

bad.text: The dollar squeeze is accelerating, and that is the tightening now: DXY 102.14 at the 98th percentile (z=1.71, acc 1.69), EURUSD at the 1st percentile, USDCAD at the 95th, USDINR at the 98th. Rising dollar = rising global funding cost.

The peso is the stress point: USDMXN +1.1% today, +7.5% on the month, z=2.82 with acceleration 2.15. EM FX broadly weaker (CEW -2.2% 1m) and EEM/SPY acceleration -2.04 — a faster, not slower, de-rating of EM beta.

The household rate got worse again: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +12bp on the week and +69bp on the month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, 100th percentile. 10-year real yield 2.87%, +44bp on the month, 33% above its 200-day. ITB and XHB sit at the 4th and 6th percentiles for a reason.

Financials are the fresh leak: GS -14.9% on the month (z=-2.11), BX -15.9%, IAI -8.5% with acceleration -1.22, KBE -6.6%, XLF -6.2% versus the index. Capital-markets beta is being marked down while the index holds.

Breadth is still at the floor despite yesterday's bounce: RSP/SPY at the 10th percentile (z=-1.42), IWM/SPY at the 14th (z=-1.87), breadth composite -17. The S&P at the 96th percentile is being carried by a handful of names.

The AI periphery keeps liquidating: NLR -17.1% on the month at the 0th percentile (z=-2.41), REMX -21.0% (0th), URA -18.8%, ORCL -16.5% with acceleration -1.56. Anything requiring debt, power or ore to deliver AI is being sold outright.

trades.name: Buy cheap index convexity into a 96th-percentile S&P
trades.line: Buy SPX Dec put spread / VIX calls — hedge costs nothing
trades.expr: SPX December 7,400/6,950 put spread, financed partly by selling a 1-month 8,050 call; or VIX Dec 20/30 call spread. Size 50-75bp of premium.
trades.thesis: The index sits at the 96th percentile and 7.1% above its 200-day while breadth is at the 10th percentile, financials are down double digits on the month and the dollar is squeezing. Protection against that configuration is priced at the bottom decile of the year.
trades.trigger: VIX 15.19 (10th percentile), VIX3M 18.08 (6th percentile), term structure 0.852 — yet SKEW jumped 5.2% to 149.19. Wings are being bid while the at-the-money is not.
trades.stop: VIX sustained below 13 with RSP/SPY reclaiming its 200-day and IWM/SPY back above the 30th percentile; otherwise premium at risk is the stop.
trades.target: VIX 22+, SPX 7,400 touched — roughly 3x on the structure.

trades.name: Short home construction into a 7.40% mortgage
trades.line: Short ITB: mortgage 7.40%, 100th pctile, still accelerating
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy ITB Jan 85 puts; alternatively short DHI against long XLV for a market-neutral version.
trades.thesis: The single most extreme series in the digest is the mortgage rate — +69bp in a month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, 100th percentile of 52 weeks. Builders bounced on that, which is the wrong reaction; affordability is deteriorating faster now than at any point this year.
trades.trigger: ITB +1.4% and XHB +0.8% yesterday with acceleration flipping positive (+0.47/+0.45) — a bounce to sell. 10-year real yield 2.87%, +44bp on the month, 33% above its 200-day.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back below 7.00%, or ITB closes above 92 (its recent breakdown shelf).
trades.target: ITB 78 (-9%); XHB/SPY to new lows below the 2nd percentile.

trades.name: Short EM beta against the S&P on the dollar squeeze
trades.line: Short EEM vs long SPY: dollar acceleration hits EM first
trades.expr: Short EEM, long equal-notional SPY. Overlay: long USD vs MXN 3-month forward for the pure FX leg.
trades.thesis: Tightening has migrated from the curve to the currency. A dollar at the 98th percentile and still accelerating is a direct hit to EM earnings, funding and flows, and the relative series are already breaking before the headline index does.
trades.trigger: EEM/SPY z=-1.25 with acceleration -2.04, -5.2% on the month. USDMXN +7.5% on the month (z=2.82, acc 2.15), USDINR at the 98th percentile, CEW -2.2%, EFA/SPY at the 0.2 percentile.
trades.stop: DXY closes below 100 or EURUSD back above 1.145; EEM/SPY reclaims its 200-day (ratio ~0.0877).

trades.name: Fade E&P beta after the crude give-back
trades.line: Short XOP: crude rolling while energy equity prints 93rd pctile
trades.expr: Short XOP, or buy XOP Dec 185 puts. Keep XLE long-side exposure if you have it — the short is the high-beta sleeve, not the integrateds.
trades.thesis: Energy equity was marked on yesterday's +3.2% WTI spike; today the barrel took it back and the refined product collapsed. E&Ps carry the full beta to that reversal with no valuation cushion after a +21.8% three-month run.
trades.trigger: WTI -1.1% to 90.44 (-5.8% on the month, acceleration -1.47), Brent -1.6%, RBOB -5.6% on the day. XOP at the 93rd percentile and 18.1% above its 200-day; XLE at the 99th percentile.
trades.stop: Brent closes above 105 or WTI above 95 (geopolitical re-rating).
trades.target: XOP 175 (-9%); XLE relative strength vs S&P rolls from +16% 3m toward flat.

trades.name: Copper miners catching up to the metal
trades.line: Long COPX/FCX: copper 95th pctile, miners -12.9% on the month
trades.expr: Long COPX; or long FCX with Jan 70 calls. Hedge with a short in GDX if you want the pure base-over-precious expression.
trades.thesis: Copper is at the 95th percentile, 8.9% above its 200-day, and copper/gold is at the 99th — yet the equity is at its 200-day after a 12.9% monthly drawdown. Either the metal is wrong or the miners are, and the metal has been leading all year (+32% over 12 months).
trades.trigger: Copper +2.8% today and +3.2% on the week; COPX -12.9% on the month with z=-1.51 and acceleration -1.33 — a stretched divergence, with FCX only -1.0% on the day.
trades.stop: Copper closes below 6.40, or COPX makes a new one-month low under 78.

trades.name: Long software against semiconductors
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: code funds itself, silicon needs capex
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH at equal notional (roughly 1.0 beta-adjusted; trim SMH leg to 0.85x if you want less net short on the AI complex).
trades.thesis: The de-grossing is hitting anything that requires capex, power or ore, and rewarding cash-generative software. The ratio has already turned and the fundamental driver — a 5.22% 10-year and 7.40% mortgages — isn't going away quickly.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +2.7% on the day, +3.0% on the week, +16.8% over three months. SOXX -3.4%, MU -4.8%, AVGO -4.3% yesterday while IGV was only -0.2% and CIBR is +13.0% on the month (z=1.62, acc 1.72).
trades.stop: Ratio back below 0.172 (-5%) or SMH reclaims its recent high with semis relative strength re-accelerating above +6% 1m.

trades.name: Brazil — the one EM with currency and equity agreeing
trades.line: Long EWZ: +14.7% on the week with the real strengthening
trades.expr: Long EWZ; add EWZ Jan 45 calls for convexity. Do not currency-hedge — the real is the point.
trades.thesis: Every other EM is being compressed by the dollar; Brazil is appreciating against it. Terms-of-trade from firm soft commodities (soybeans +25.6% ytd, corn +13.6%) plus a disinflating currency make this the only clean EM long while DXY sits at the 98th percentile.
trades.trigger: EWZ +14.7% on the week, +10.3% on the month, 97th percentile; BVSP z=1.69 with +8.7% relative to the S&P on the month; USDBRL -4.0% on the week and -8.5% ytd.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.25, or EWZ closes below 39.
